```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("Packages.R")

blue <- "#3B82F6"
red <- "#EF4444"
grey <- "#64748B"

set.seed(2026)

# ============================================================
# HELPERS
# ============================================================

to_numeric <- function(x) {
  suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(x)))
}

to_binary <- function(x, name) {
  y <- to_numeric(x)

  if (
    any(!is.na(x) & is.na(y)) ||
    any(!is.na(y) & !y %in% c(0, 1))
  ) {
    stop("Invalid binary coding in: ", name)
  }

  y
}

# Odds ratios and Wald 95% confidence intervals
get_or_table <- function(model) {

  coefficients <- summary(model)$coefficients

  tibble::tibble(
    Variable = rownames(coefficients),
    Estimate = coefficients[, "Estimate"],
    SE = coefficients[, "Std. Error"],
    OR = exp(Estimate),
    CI_lower = exp(Estimate - 1.96 * SE),
    CI_upper = exp(Estimate + 1.96 * SE),
    p_value = coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
  )
}

extract_protein <- function(model, label) {

  get_or_table(model) %>%
    filter(Variable == "Protein_01") %>%
    mutate(Model = label) %>%
    select(Model, OR, CI_lower, CI_upper, p_value)
}

show_or_table <- function(results, caption) {

  results %>%
    mutate(
      across(
        any_of(c("OR", "CI_lower", "CI_upper")),
        ~ round(.x, 3)
      ),
      across(
        any_of("p_value"),
        ~ signif(.x, 3)
      )
    ) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = caption)
}

check_model <- function(model, label) {

  valid <- isTRUE(model$converged) &&
    all(is.finite(coef(model))) &&
    all(is.finite(vcov(model)))

  if (!valid) {
    warning("Potentially unstable model: ", label)
  }

  valid
}

theme_report <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
}

# ============================================================
# PREDICTION PERFORMANCE FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================

# AUC calculated using the rank-based definition
calculate_auc <- function(y, p) {

  keep <- is.finite(p) & !is.na(y)
  y <- y[keep]
  p <- p[keep]

  n1 <- sum(y == 1)
  n0 <- sum(y == 0)

  if (n1 == 0 || n0 == 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  ranks <- rank(p, ties.method = "average")

  (
    sum(ranks[y == 1]) -
      n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2
  ) / (n1 * n0)
}

calculate_metrics <- function(y, p) {

  keep <- !is.na(y) & is.finite(p)
  y <- y[keep]
  p <- p[keep]

  p_safe <- pmin(pmax(p, 1e-12), 1 - 1e-12)

  tibble::tibble(
    Patients = length(y),
    AKI_events = sum(y == 1),
    AUC = calculate_auc(y, p),
    Brier = mean((y - p)^2),
    Log_loss = -mean(
      y * log(p_safe) +
        (1 - y) * log(1 - p_safe)
    )
  )
}

# Reproducible stratified training/test split
stratified_split <- function(y, train_fraction = 0.8) {

  train_ids <- unlist(
    lapply(
      split(seq_along(y), y),
      function(ids) {

        n_train <- floor(
          length(ids) * train_fraction
        )

        n_train <- max(
          1,
          min(n_train, length(ids) - 1)
        )

        sample(ids, n_train)
      }
    ),
    use.names = FALSE
  )

  sort(train_ids)
}

# Reproducible stratified CV folds
stratified_folds <- function(y, k) {

  fold <- integer(length(y))

  for (group in unique(y)) {

    ids <- which(y == group)

    fold[ids] <- sample(
      rep(seq_len(k), length.out = length(ids))
    )
  }

  fold
}

# Standardized predictions over patient covariates
standardized_curve <- function(model, sample_data, grid) {

  bind_rows(
    lapply(grid, function(p) {

      new_data <- sample_data %>%
        mutate(Protein_01 = p / 0.1)

      tibble::tibble(
        Protein = p,
        Probability = mean(
          predict(
            model,
            newdata = new_data,
            type = "response"
          )
        )
      )
    })
  )
}

# ============================================================
# DATA VALIDATION
# ============================================================

required_vars <- c(
  "AKI_any",
  "AKI_any_early",
  "AKI_any_sensitivity_worst_case",
  "Protein_intake__d1_4",
  "EuroScore2",
  "Duration_of_cardiopulmonary_bypass_minutes",
  "BMI",
  "days_onexclusive_oral_feeding",
  "died_in_ICU"
)

missing_vars <- setdiff(required_vars, names(data))

if (length(missing_vars) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing columns: ",
    paste(missing_vars, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

regression_data <- data %>%
  transmute(
    AKI_primary = to_binary(AKI_any, "AKI_any"),

    AKI_day56 = to_binary(
      AKI_any_early,
      "AKI_any_early"
    ),

    AKI_worst = to_binary(
      AKI_any_sensitivity_worst_case,
      "AKI_any_sensitivity_worst_case"
    ),

    Protein = to_numeric(Protein_intake__d1_4),
    EuroScore2 = to_numeric(EuroScore2),

    CPB = to_numeric(
      Duration_of_cardiopulmonary_bypass_minutes
    ),

    BMI = to_numeric(BMI),

    Oral_days = to_numeric(
      days_onexclusive_oral_feeding
    ),

    ICU_death = case_when(
      as.character(died_in_ICU) == "Yes" ~ 1L,
      as.character(died_in_ICU) == "No" ~ 0L,
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Protein_01 = Protein / 0.1,
    CPB_30 = CPB / 30
  )

if (
  any(regression_data$Protein < 0, na.rm = TRUE) ||
  any(regression_data$CPB < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
) {
  stop("Negative protein intake or CPB duration detected.")
}

formula_unadjusted <- AKI_primary ~ Protein_01

formula_core <- AKI_primary ~
  Protein_01 + EuroScore2 + CPB_30
```

# 1. Research Objective

## Research Question

Is artificially administered protein intake during ICU days 1–4 associated with AKI after day 4, after adjustment for preoperative risk and surgical complexity?

Artificial protein intake was not randomized. The analysis therefore estimates an observational association rather than a causal treatment effect.

## Outcomes and Covariates

| Role | Variable | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Exposure | `Protein_intake__d1_4` | Mean artificial protein intake, g/kg/day |
| Primary outcome | `AKI_any` | New AKI after day 4 |
| Secondary outcome | `AKI_any_early` | New AKI on days 5–6 |
| Sensitivity outcome | `AKI_any_sensitivity_worst_case` | Worst-case handling of ICU death |
| Core covariate | `EuroScore2` | Preoperative surgical risk |
| Core covariate | CPB duration | Intraoperative exposure |
| Additional covariate | `BMI` | Preoperative patient characteristic |
| Exploratory covariate | Oral-feeding days | Feeding status during days 1–4 |

The primary model uses continuous artificial protein intake, EuroSCORE II and CPB duration.

Protein associations are reported per 0.1 g/kg/day; CPB associations per 30 minutes.

# 2. Analysis Population

## 2.1 Available Observations

```{r population-summary}
population_summary <- regression_data %>%
  summarise(
    Patients = n(),
    Primary_events = sum(AKI_primary == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Secondary_events = sum(AKI_day56 == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Worst_case_events = sum(AKI_worst == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

knitr::kable(
  population_summary,
  caption = "Study population and AKI events"
)
```

## 2.2 Complete Cases for the Core Model

Both primary development models use the same complete-case sample.

```{r complete-cases}
model_data <- regression_data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(AKI_primary),
    !is.na(Protein_01),
    !is.na(EuroScore2),
    !is.na(CPB_30)
  )

n_events <- sum(model_data$AKI_primary == 1)
n_nonevents <- sum(model_data$AKI_primary == 0)

if (n_events < 2 || n_nonevents < 2) {
  stop(
    "Too few events or non-events for ",
    "a training/test split."
  )
}

model_sample_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  Measure = c(
    "Total eligible patients",
    "Complete cases",
    "Excluded due to missing core model variables",
    "AKI events",
    "Non-AKI patients",
    "AKI proportion (%)"
  ),
  Value = c(
    as.character(nrow(regression_data)),
    as.character(nrow(model_data)),
    as.character(
      nrow(regression_data) - nrow(model_data)
    ),
    as.character(n_events),
    as.character(n_nonevents),
    sprintf(
      "%.1f",
      100 * mean(model_data$AKI_primary)
    )
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  model_sample_summary,
  align = c("l", "r"),
  caption = "Primary model analysis sample"
)
```

# 3. Training and Test Sets

## 3.1 Stratified Split

We randomly allocate approximately 80% of patients to training and 20% to testing, stratified by primary AKI status.

Stratification maintains representation of both AKI and non-AKI patients in each subset.

The test set is not used for model fitting or cross-validation.

```{r train-test-split}
set.seed(2026)

train_ids <- stratified_split(
  model_data$AKI_primary,
  train_fraction = 0.8
)

train_data <- model_data[train_ids, , drop = FALSE]

test_data <- model_data[
  -train_ids,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

split_summary <- bind_rows(
  train_data %>%
    summarise(
      Sample = "Training",
      Patients = n(),
      AKI_events = sum(AKI_primary == 1),
      Non_AKI = sum(AKI_primary == 0)
    ),

  test_data %>%
    summarise(
      Sample = "Testing",
      Patients = n(),
      AKI_events = sum(AKI_primary == 1),
      Non_AKI = sum(AKI_primary == 0)
    )
)

knitr::kable(
  split_summary,
  caption = "Stratified training and test sets"
)

if (min(
  sum(test_data$AKI_primary == 1),
  sum(test_data$AKI_primary == 0)
) < 5) {
  cat(
    "\n\n**Caution:** The test set contains fewer than ",
    "five patients in at least one outcome class. ",
    "Test performance estimates may be very unstable."
  )
}
```

The split is used for evaluating prediction performance. It is not necessary for unbiased estimation of a prespecified observational regression association.

# 4. Model Development on Training Data

## 4.1 Unadjusted Logistic Regression

```{r train-unadjusted}
model_unadjusted_train <- glm(
  formula_unadjusted,
  data = train_data,
  family = binomial()
)

check_model(
  model_unadjusted_train,
  "Training unadjusted model"
)

show_or_table(
  get_or_table(model_unadjusted_train) %>%
    filter(Variable != "(Intercept)"),
  "Unadjusted logistic regression: training sample"
)
```

## 4.2 Core Adjusted Logistic Regression

```{r train-adjusted}
model_adjusted_train <- glm(
  formula_core,
  data = train_data,
  family = binomial()
)

check_model(
  model_adjusted_train,
  "Training adjusted model"
)

show_or_table(
  get_or_table(model_adjusted_train) %>%
    filter(Variable != "(Intercept)"),
  "Adjusted logistic regression: training sample"
)
```

## 4.3 Protein Association Comparison

```{r train-model-comparison, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
train_comparison <- bind_rows(
  extract_protein(
    model_unadjusted_train,
    "Unadjusted"
  ),
  extract_protein(
    model_adjusted_train,
    "Adjusted: EuroSCORE II + CPB"
  )
)

show_or_table(
  train_comparison,
  "Protein association in training models"
)

p_train_forest <- ggplot(
  train_comparison,
  aes(x = OR, y = Model)
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = grey
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(
      x = CI_lower,
      xend = CI_upper,
      yend = Model
    ),
    linewidth = 0.9,
    color = blue
  ) +
  geom_point(
    color = blue,
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "Unadjusted vs Adjusted Protein Association",
    subtitle = "Training sample; OR per 0.1 g/kg/day",
    x = "Odds ratio (log scale)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_report()

print(p_train_forest)
```

The estimated change between models may partly reflect measured risk differences. Changes in logistic-regression odds ratios cannot be attributed entirely to confounding because odds ratios are non-collapsible.

# 5. Cross-Validation

## 5.1 Stratified K-Fold Cross-Validation

Cross-validation evaluates how well the predefined model performs on patients excluded from each fold's model fitting.

For each fold:

1. Fit the model using the remaining training folds.
2. Predict AKI probabilities for the excluded fold.
3. Collect the out-of-fold predictions.
4. Calculate performance metrics.

The held-out test set remains untouched throughout this process.

```{r cross-validation}
set.seed(2026)

# At most five folds, respecting the smallest outcome class
k <- min(
  5L,
  as.integer(min(table(train_data$AKI_primary)))
)

if (k < 2L) {
  stop(
    "Insufficient AKI events or non-events ",
    "for stratified cross-validation."
  )
}

cv_folds <- stratified_folds(
  train_data$AKI_primary,
  k
)

cv_predictions <- train_data %>%
  mutate(
    Fold = cv_folds,
    CV_unadjusted = NA_real_,
    CV_adjusted = NA_real_
  )

for (fold in seq_len(k)) {

  cv_train <- train_data[
    cv_folds != fold,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  cv_valid <- train_data[
    cv_folds == fold,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  cv_model_unadjusted <- glm(
    formula_unadjusted,
    data = cv_train,
    family = binomial()
  )

  cv_model_adjusted <- glm(
    formula_core,
    data = cv_train,
    family = binomial()
  )

  cv_predictions$CV_unadjusted[cv_folds == fold] <-
    predict(
      cv_model_unadjusted,
      newdata = cv_valid,
      type = "response"
    )

  cv_predictions$CV_adjusted[cv_folds == fold] <-
    predict(
      cv_model_adjusted,
      newdata = cv_valid,
      type = "response"
    )
}

# Evaluate pooled out-of-fold predictions
cv_results <- bind_rows(
  calculate_metrics(
    cv_predictions$AKI_primary,
    cv_predictions$CV_unadjusted
  ) %>%
    mutate(Model = "Unadjusted"),

  calculate_metrics(
    cv_predictions$AKI_primary,
    cv_predictions$CV_adjusted
  ) %>%
    mutate(Model = "Core adjusted")
) %>%
  select(
    Model,
    Patients,
    AKI_events,
    AUC,
    Brier,
    Log_loss
  )

knitr::kable(
  cv_results,
  digits = 3,
  caption = paste0(
    k,
    "-fold cross-validation performance"
  )
)
```

AUC measures discrimination. The Brier score measures the mean squared error of predicted probabilities, and log loss penalizes incorrect confident predictions.

For AUC, higher is better; for Brier score and log loss, lower is better.

These metrics assess prediction, not whether the protein coefficient has a causal interpretation.

## 5.2 Cross-Validated Calibration

```{r cv-calibration, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
cv_calibration <- cv_predictions %>%
  transmute(
    Observed = AKI_primary,
    Unadjusted = CV_unadjusted,
    Adjusted = CV_adjusted
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Unadjusted, Adjusted),
    names_to = "Model",
    values_to = "Predicted"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Model) %>%
  mutate(
    Bin = dplyr::ntile(
      Predicted,
      min(5L, n())
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(Model, Bin) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_predicted = mean(Predicted),
    Observed_risk = mean(Observed),
    Patients = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

p_cv_calibration <- ggplot(
  cv_calibration,
  aes(
    x = Mean_predicted,
    y = Observed_risk
  )
) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0,
    slope = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = grey
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(size = Patients),
    color = blue
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Model) +
  coord_equal(
    xlim = c(0, 1),
    ylim = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    title = "Cross-Validated Calibration",
    subtitle = "Observed versus out-of-fold predicted AKI",
    x = "Mean predicted probability",
    y = "Observed AKI proportion",
    size = "Patients"
  ) +
  theme_report()

print(p_cv_calibration)
```

With limited events, individual calibration bins can contain few AKI cases. This plot is exploratory and should not be interpreted as a precise calibration assessment.

# 6. Held-Out Test-Set Evaluation

Both training models are applied to patients who were excluded from model development and cross-validation.

No test-set observations are used to refit either model.

```{r test-evaluation}
test_predictions <- test_data %>%
  mutate(
    Pred_unadjusted = predict(
      model_unadjusted_train,
      newdata = test_data,
      type = "response"
    ),

    Pred_adjusted = predict(
      model_adjusted_train,
      newdata = test_data,
      type = "response"
    )
  )

test_results <- bind_rows(
  calculate_metrics(
    test_predictions$AKI_primary,
    test_predictions$Pred_unadjusted
  ) %>%
    mutate(Model = "Unadjusted"),

  calculate_metrics(
    test_predictions$AKI_primary,
    test_predictions$Pred_adjusted
  ) %>%
    mutate(Model = "Core adjusted")
) %>%
  select(
    Model,
    Patients,
    AKI_events,
    AUC,
    Brier,
    Log_loss
  )

knitr::kable(
  test_results,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Performance on the held-out test set"
)
```

## 6.1 Cross-Validation versus Test Performance

```{r validation-comparison}
validation_comparison <- bind_rows(
  cv_results %>%
    mutate(Evaluation = "Cross-validation"),

  test_results %>%
    mutate(Evaluation = "Test set")
) %>%
  select(
    Evaluation,
    Model,
    Patients,
    AKI_events,
    AUC,
    Brier,
    Log_loss
  )

knitr::kable(
  validation_comparison,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Internal validation performance comparison"
)
```

Test performance may be unstable if the test set is small. A favorable result on one random split is not sufficient to establish external validity.

# 7. Final Primary Association Analysis

For the scientific association analysis, we now refit the prespecified models using **all complete cases**.

This improves precision compared with reporting coefficients from the training subset alone.

The following models are intended for inference about the observed protein–AKI association, not as independent test-set predictions.

## 7.1 Final Unadjusted and Adjusted Models

```{r final-models}
model_unadjusted <- glm(
  formula_unadjusted,
  data = model_data,
  family = binomial()
)

model_adjusted <- glm(
  formula_core,
  data = model_data,
  family = binomial()
)

check_model(
  model_unadjusted,
  "Final unadjusted model"
)

check_model(
  model_adjusted,
  "Final adjusted model"
)

final_results <- bind_rows(
  extract_protein(
    model_unadjusted,
    "Unadjusted"
  ),
  extract_protein(
    model_adjusted,
    "Core adjusted"
  )
)

show_or_table(
  final_results,
  "Final protein association using all complete cases"
)

show_or_table(
  get_or_table(model_adjusted) %>%
    filter(Variable != "(Intercept)"),
  "Final adjusted regression coefficients"
)
```

## 7.2 Observed Outcomes and Adjusted Fitted Curve

Blue points represent patients without AKI and red points represent patients with AKI.

The black curve shows the model-estimated AKI probability, standardized over the observed EuroSCORE II and CPB duration distributions.

```{r observed-fitted-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.5}
protein_grid <- seq(
  min(model_data$Protein),
  max(model_data$Protein),
  length.out = 150
)

fitted_curve <- standardized_curve(
  model_adjusted,
  model_data,
  protein_grid
)

p_observed_fitted <- ggplot() +

  geom_jitter(
    data = model_data,
    aes(
      x = Protein,
      y = AKI_primary,
      color = factor(AKI_primary)
    ),
    width = 0,
    height = 0.035,
    alpha = 0.35,
    size = 1.7
  ) +

  geom_line(
    data = fitted_curve,
    aes(
      x = Protein,
      y = Probability
    ),
    color = "#111827",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "0" = blue,
      "1" = red
    ),
    labels = c(
      "No AKI",
      "AKI"
    ),
    name = "Observed outcome"
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
    labels = scales::percent
  ) +

  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(-0.05, 1.05)
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Observed AKI and Adjusted Model Predictions",
    subtitle = "Individual observations and standardized fitted probability",
    x = "Artificial protein intake (g/kg/day)",
    y = "AKI outcome / predicted probability"
  ) +

  theme_report() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(p_observed_fitted)
```

The fitted curve is not an observed risk curve or a causal dose-response estimate. Predictions at protein doses with poor covariate overlap require particular caution.

# 8. Model Diagnostics

The following diagnostics examine residual behavior, predictive calibration, leverage and influential observations.

Because AKI is binary, logistic regression does not require normally distributed residuals.

## 8.1 Four Diagnostic Plots

```{r four-diagnostic-plots, fig.width=12, fig.height=9}
diagnostic_data <- tibble::tibble(
  Observation = seq_len(nrow(model_data)),
  Observed = model_data$AKI_primary,

  Fitted = fitted(model_adjusted),

  Deviance_residual = residuals(
    model_adjusted,
    type = "deviance"
  ),

  Standardized_residual = rstandard(
    model_adjusted,
    type = "deviance"
  ),

  Leverage = hatvalues(model_adjusted),
  Cooks_distance = cooks.distance(model_adjusted)
)

# 1. Deviance residuals versus fitted probabilities
p_diag1 <- ggplot(
  diagnostic_data,
  aes(
    x = Fitted,
    y = Deviance_residual
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    color = blue,
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 1.6
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = grey
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "1. Residuals vs Fitted",
    x = "Fitted AKI probability",
    y = "Deviance residual"
  ) +
  theme_report()

# 2. Observed versus predicted AKI
n_bins <- min(
  10L,
  nrow(diagnostic_data),
  length(unique(diagnostic_data$Fitted))
)

binned_data <- diagnostic_data %>%
  mutate(
    Bin = dplyr::ntile(Fitted, n_bins)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Bin) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_predicted = mean(Fitted),
    Observed_AKI = mean(Observed),
    Patients = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

p_diag2 <- ggplot(
  binned_data,
  aes(
    x = Mean_predicted,
    y = Observed_AKI
  )
) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0,
    slope = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = grey
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(size = Patients),
    color = blue
  ) +
  coord_equal(
    xlim = c(0, 1),
    ylim = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    title = "2. Observed vs Predicted AKI",
    x = "Mean predicted AKI probability",
    y = "Observed AKI proportion",
    size = "Patients"
  ) +
  theme_report()

# 3. Residuals versus leverage
p_diag3 <- ggplot(
  diagnostic_data,
  aes(
    x = Leverage,
    y = Standardized_residual
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    aes(size = Cooks_distance),
    color = blue,
    alpha = 0.55
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = grey
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "3. Residuals vs Leverage",
    x = "Leverage",
    y = "Standardized deviance residual",
    size = "Cook's D"
  ) +
  theme_report()

# 4. Cook's distance
p_diag4 <- ggplot(
  diagnostic_data,
  aes(
    x = Observation,
    y = Cooks_distance
  )
) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(
      xend = Observation,
      yend = 0
    ),
    color = blue,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 4 / nrow(model_data),
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = red
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "4. Cook's Distance",
    subtitle = "Dashed line: 4/n screening heuristic",
    x = "Observation index",
    y = "Cook's distance"
  ) +
  theme_report()

p_diagnostics <- patchwork::wrap_plots(
  p_diag1,
  p_diag2,
  p_diag3,
  p_diag4,
  ncol = 2
) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Core Adjusted Logistic Regression Diagnostics"
  )

print(p_diagnostics)
```

## 8.2 Diagnostic Summary

```{r diagnostic-summary}
diagnostic_summary <- diagnostic_data %>%
  summarise(
    Patients = n(),
    Maximum_Cooks_D = max(Cooks_distance),
    Above_4_over_n = sum(
      Cooks_distance > 4 / nrow(model_data)
    ),
    Maximum_leverage = max(Leverage)
  )

knitr::kable(
  diagnostic_summary %>%
    mutate(
      Maximum_Cooks_D = round(Maximum_Cooks_D, 4),
      Maximum_leverage = round(Maximum_leverage, 4)
    ),
  caption = "Influence diagnostic summary"
)
```

Observations with high influence require investigation, not automatic removal. The plots do not establish the absence of confounding or validate every model assumption.

## 8.3 Exploratory Nonlinearity Assessment

A logistic regression assumes linearity of continuous predictors on the log-odds scale.

We investigate whether a more flexible protein relationship is supported by the data. This comparison is exploratory.

```{r nonlinearity-check}
sufficient_information <- (
  sum(model_data$AKI_primary == 1) >= 40 &&
  sum(model_data$AKI_primary == 0) >= 40 &&
  length(unique(model_data$Protein_01)) >= 5
)

if (sufficient_information) {

  model_spline <- glm(
    AKI_primary ~
      splines::ns(Protein_01, df = 3) +
      EuroScore2 +
      CPB_30,
    data = model_data,
    family = binomial()
  )

  knitr::kable(
    as.data.frame(
      anova(
        model_adjusted,
        model_spline,
        test = "Chisq"
      )
    ),
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Exploratory comparison of linear and spline protein effects"
  )

} else {

  cat(
    "The exploratory spline analysis was not fitted ",
    "because event counts or exposure variation ",
    "were limited."
  )
}
```

The threshold is a pragmatic condition for attempting an exploratory fit, not a guarantee of model adequacy. EuroSCORE II and CPB duration may also require functional-form checks.

# 9. Additional Covariate Analyses

## 9.1 BMI Adjustment

The following comparison evaluates whether including BMI changes the estimated protein association.

Both models use the same BMI-complete sample.

```{r bmi-adjustment}
bmi_data <- regression_data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(AKI_primary),
    !is.na(Protein_01),
    !is.na(EuroScore2),
    !is.na(CPB_30),
    !is.na(BMI)
  )

if (
  n_distinct(bmi_data$AKI_primary) == 2 &&
  n_distinct(bmi_data$BMI) > 1
) {

  model_core_bmi <- glm(
    formula_core,
    data = bmi_data,
    family = binomial()
  )

  model_bmi <- glm(
    AKI_primary ~
      Protein_01 +
      EuroScore2 +
      CPB_30 +
      BMI,
    data = bmi_data,
    family = binomial()
  )

  bmi_results <- bind_rows(
    extract_protein(
      model_core_bmi,
      "Core model"
    ),
    extract_protein(
      model_bmi,
      "Core model + BMI"
    )
  )

  show_or_table(
    bmi_results,
    "Sensitivity to BMI adjustment"
  )

  cat(
    "\n\nSample:",
    nrow(bmi_data),
    "patients;",
    sum(bmi_data$AKI_primary == 1),
    "AKI events."
  )

} else {

  cat("Insufficient data for BMI model comparison.")
}
```

## 9.2 Exploratory Oral-Feeding Adjustment

Oral feeding was measured concurrently with artificial protein intake. It may reflect evolving illness and recovery rather than a conventional pre-exposure confounder.

Consequently, this model is exploratory and does not necessarily provide a less biased estimate.

```{r oral-adjustment}
oral_data <- regression_data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(AKI_primary),
    !is.na(Protein_01),
    !is.na(EuroScore2),
    !is.na(CPB_30),
    !is.na(Oral_days),
    Oral_days %in% 0:4
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Oral_days = factor(
      Oral_days,
      levels = 0:4
    ),

    Protein_group = factor(
      if_else(
        Protein == 0,
        "Zero",
        "Positive"
      ),
      levels = c("Zero", "Positive")
    )
  )

oral_overlap <- oral_data %>%
  count(
    Oral_days,
    Protein_group,
    name = "Patients"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    Oral_days,
    Protein_group,
    fill = list(Patients = 0)
  )

knitr::kable(
  oral_overlap,
  caption = "Exposure overlap by oral-feeding days"
)

if (
  n_distinct(oral_data$AKI_primary) == 2 &&
  n_distinct(oral_data$Oral_days) > 1 &&
  n_distinct(oral_data$Protein_01) > 1
) {

  model_core_oral <- glm(
    formula_core,
    data = oral_data,
    family = binomial()
  )

  model_oral <- glm(
    AKI_primary ~
      Protein_01 +
      EuroScore2 +
      CPB_30 +
      Oral_days,
    data = oral_data,
    family = binomial()
  )

  oral_results <- bind_rows(
    extract_protein(
      model_core_oral,
      "Core model"
    ),
    extract_protein(
      model_oral,
      "Core model + oral feeding"
    )
  )

  show_or_table(
    oral_results,
    "Exploratory oral-feeding adjustment"
  )

} else {

  cat("Insufficient variation for oral-feeding model.")
}
```

# 10. Secondary and Worst-Case Outcome Analyses

## 10.1 Outcome Validation

Before comparing outcomes, we verify consistency between the secondary indicator and primary AKI.

```{r outcome-validation}
nesting_errors <- regression_data %>%
  filter(
    AKI_day56 == 1,
    AKI_primary == 0
  ) %>%
  nrow()

outcome_validation <- tibble::tibble(
  Check = "Day 5-6 AKI without primary AKI",
  Patients = nesting_errors
)

knitr::kable(
  outcome_validation,
  caption = "AKI outcome consistency"
)
```

The after-day-6 exploratory outcome is not modeled here because its validity depends on confirming that the day 5–6 indicator represents the first occurrence of new AKI.

## 10.2 Worst-Case Classification Check

```{r worst-case-validation}
reclassification_table <- regression_data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(AKI_primary),
    !is.na(AKI_worst)
  ) %>%
  count(
    AKI_primary,
    AKI_worst,
    name = "Patients"
  )

knitr::kable(
  reclassification_table,
  caption = "Primary versus worst-case AKI classification"
)

death_check <- regression_data %>%
  filter(
    AKI_primary == 0,
    AKI_worst == 1
  ) %>%
  count(
    ICU_death,
    name = "Patients"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Death_status = case_when(
      ICU_death == 1 ~ "Died in ICU",
      ICU_death == 0 ~ "Survived ICU",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(Death_status, Patients)

knitr::kable(
  death_check,
  caption = "ICU death among reclassified patients"
)
```

The worst-case indicator comes directly from the supplied dataset. Patients reclassified as AKI cases are not necessarily patients with documented kidney injury.

## 10.3 Adjusted Models Across Outcomes

The three outcome models use a common complete-case sample for comparability.

```{r outcome-models}
common_data <- regression_data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(AKI_primary),
    !is.na(AKI_day56),
    !is.na(AKI_worst),
    !is.na(Protein_01),
    !is.na(EuroScore2),
    !is.na(CPB_30)
  )

if (
  n_distinct(common_data$AKI_primary) < 2 ||
  n_distinct(common_data$AKI_day56) < 2 ||
  n_distinct(common_data$AKI_worst) < 2
) {
  stop(
    "One of the AKI outcomes has insufficient ",
    "variation in the common sample."
  )
}

model_primary_common <- glm(
  AKI_primary ~
    Protein_01 + EuroScore2 + CPB_30,
  data = common_data,
  family = binomial()
)

model_secondary_common <- glm(
  AKI_day56 ~
    Protein_01 + EuroScore2 + CPB_30,
  data = common_data,
  family = binomial()
)

model_worst_common <- glm(
  AKI_worst ~
    Protein_01 + EuroScore2 + CPB_30,
  data = common_data,
  family = binomial()
)

check_model(
  model_primary_common,
  "Primary outcome"
)

check_model(
  model_secondary_common,
  "Secondary outcome"
)

check_model(
  model_worst_common,
  "Worst-case outcome"
)

outcome_comparison <- bind_rows(
  extract_protein(
    model_primary_common,
    "Primary: AKI after day 4"
  ),
  extract_protein(
    model_secondary_common,
    "Secondary: AKI days 5-6"
  ),
  extract_protein(
    model_worst_common,
    "Worst-case AKI"
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    Patients = nrow(common_data),

    AKI_events = c(
      sum(common_data$AKI_primary == 1),
      sum(common_data$AKI_day56 == 1),
      sum(common_data$AKI_worst == 1)
    )
  )

show_or_table(
  outcome_comparison,
  "Adjusted protein association across AKI outcomes"
)
```

## 10.4 Outcome Comparison Forest Plot

```{r outcome-forest, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
p_outcome_forest <- ggplot(
  outcome_comparison,
  aes(
    x = OR,
    y = Model
  )
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = grey
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(
      x = CI_lower,
      xend = CI_upper,
      yend = Model
    ),
    color = blue,
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_point(
    color = blue,
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "Adjusted Protein Association Across AKI Outcomes",
    subtitle = "Common sample; OR per 0.1 g/kg/day",
    x = "Adjusted odds ratio (log scale)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_report()

print(p_outcome_forest)
```

These models examine associations under different endpoint definitions. Their coefficients should not be interpreted as direct estimates of the causal effect of artificial protein intake.

# 11. Discussion and Limitations

## Interpretation Framework

The analysis should address:

1. The magnitude, direction and uncertainty of the primary protein association.
2. Differences between unadjusted and adjusted models.
3. Cross-validated and held-out predictive performance.
4. Whether the model specification is supported by diagnostic results.
5. The sensitivity of the association to BMI, oral feeding, and AKI definitions.

## Important Limitations

**Confounding by indication:** Artificial protein was prescribed according to clinical judgment rather than randomized.

**Residual confounding:** EuroSCORE II and CPB duration do not fully capture postoperative ICU severity.

**Selection bias:** The cohort consists of patients with prolonged ICU stays, potentially selected according to severity and complications.

**Limited exposure overlap:** Patients with four exclusively oral-feeding days received no artificially administered protein.

**Competing events:** ICU death can prevent subsequent AKI from being observed. Worst-case classification examines one assumption but does not resolve the competing-risk problem.

**Internal validation:** Cross-validation and a test split describe predictive performance. Neither removes confounding nor validates causal interpretations.

**Sample size:** The precision of all models depends on the numbers of events and non-events, especially within training, validation, and test subsets.

## Conclusion

The primary adjusted regression estimates the association between artificial protein intake and subsequent AKI, conditional on EuroSCORE II and CPB duration.

Cross-validation and held-out testing provide additional information about predictive performance. The final association models use all complete cases to avoid unnecessarily sacrificing statistical precision.

Interpretation should prioritize effect sizes, confidence intervals, model adequacy, clinical plausibility and the limitations of the observational design.
